title: My battery dies too quickly
summary: The radio runs flat in hours rather than days.

steps.question: Is WiFi turned off on the radio?
steps.help: Settings, then Network, shows whether WiFi is enabled. It is off unless you turned it on.

steps.title: Turn WiFi off
steps.body: WiFi uses more power than everything else on the board combined. Keep it for radios that stay plugged in.
steps: Turn WiFi off and save. The radio restarts and goes back to Bluetooth.

steps.question: Is the radio's GPS off, or set to update only every few minutes?
steps.help: Settings, then Position, shows the GPS mode and the update interval. A radio without a GPS module counts as off.

steps.title: Make the GPS work less
steps.body: A GPS that is always searching, especially indoors where it cannot get a fix, is a steady drain.
steps: If the radio does not move, set the GPS mode to disabled. You can set a fixed position instead, or let the app share your phone's location.
If you do need it, lengthen the GPS update interval to a few minutes or more.
Keep Smart Position on, so the radio only reports when it has moved.

links.label: Position sharing in the setup guide

steps.question: Does the screen switch itself off within a minute?
steps.help: Answer yes if the radio has no screen.

steps.title: Shorten the screen timeout
steps.body: A screen left on drains a small battery noticeably.
steps: Set the screen-on time to 30 or 60 seconds.
Turn off the automatic carousel, which keeps waking the screen.

steps.question: Is your radio built on an nRF52 chip, rather than an ESP32?
steps.help: RAK WisBlock, LilyGo T-Echo and Seeed T1000-E radios are nRF52. Heltec V3 and LilyGo T-Beam radios are ESP32. If you are not sure, answer no.

steps.title: Expect about a day from an ESP32 radio
steps.body: ESP32 boards use several times the power of nRF52 boards even when idle. A day or less on a small battery is normal for them, not a fault.
steps: In Settings, then Power, turn on power saving. The radio sleeps when idle, and the app may take a little longer to reconnect.
Fit a larger battery if the case allows it, or carry a USB power bank.
For a radio that has to run for days, or on solar, choose an nRF52 board.

steps.question: Is the battery 1000 mAh or larger, and less than a few years old?
steps.help: The capacity is printed on the battery. Cells that have been run completely flat many times hold far less than the label says.

steps.title: Fit a larger or newer battery
steps.body: The small cells sold with some radios only last a few hours however the radio is set up.
steps: Replace the battery with the largest one that fits your case and uses the same connector.
Check the polarity of the connector before plugging it in. It is not standardized, and a reversed battery can destroy the board.

steps.title: Ask in Discord
steps.body: If the battery still drains fast, a setting or a hardware fault may be keeping the radio awake. Others with the same board can compare numbers.
include: The battery's capacity and roughly how old it is
How many hours it runs on a full charge
The device role, and your GPS, WiFi and power saving settings
